run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T03:45:51Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is driven by a short burst of failed checkout requests, not by errors originating in the proxy itself. frontend-proxy's only error spans are on the 'ingress' (and 'router frontend egress') operations, and the failed requests are POST /api/checkout: the frontend's error counter for POST /api/checkout (and its grpc client span to oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder) jumps from 36 to 95 between the 03:47:00 and 03:49:00 samples, exactly matching 59 failed PlaceOrder RPCs at checkout, each of which also failed checkout's client call to oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (checkout's Charge error counter rises 0 -> 37 -> 59 and then stops). Payment's own Charge counters record no errors and the payment log lines read contain only 'Charge request received.'/'Transaction complete.', but payment served no Charge requests between its start at 03:46:11 and 03:48:18.976, while its Deployment was rolled (a kubectl rollout restart at 03:46:08: new ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4, old pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 deleted at 03:46:11, identical image/env, only the restartedAt annotation differs). The payment Deployment runs 1 replica with no readiness/liveness/startup probe, so the Service can send traffic to the new pod before its process accepts connections; the failed Charge calls therefore never reached payment (no payment server spans, payment error rate 0) and failed fast (no latency shift in the Charge duration histogram), consistent with transport-level failure during the restart. frontend-proxy's error ratio rose from 0.00073/0.000199 (15-minute windows ending 03:45:27Z) to 70 errors against 6848.89 UNSET ingress spans (~1%, matching the alert's stated 0.0111) over 03:45:27-03:55:27, and the error counters are flat from the 03:49:00 sample onward. The non-default flagd paymentFailure='100%' value is a plausible but unsupported alternative cause: payment emitted no error spans, handled no flag ResolveFloat calls in the window, and every charge it logged completed.

claims.text: In the 22 minutes ending 2026-11-15T04:07:27Z, frontend-proxy's span counter shows STATUS_CODE_ERROR only on span_name='ingress' (increase 68.94) and span_name='router frontend egress' (62.57), against 8656.39 and 8658.51 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans; no other frontend-proxy operation has error spans.

Error spans by service (increase over 03:45:27-04:07:27) were: frontend 250.29, frontend-proxy 131.51, checkout 46.44, payment 0, accounting 0, and about 1.06 each for ad, fraud-detection and recommendation; no error series were returned for cart, currency, email, image-provider, kafka, product-catalog, quote or shipping, so their error status in this window is unknown rather than zero.

The cumulative counters place the burst precisely: frontend-proxy 'ingress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR went 489 (flat through 03:45) -> 490 at 03:46 -> 529 at 03:48 -> 550 at 03:49 -> 555 at 03:58, and frontend 'POST /api/checkout' STATUS_CODE_ERROR went 36 (flat 03:40-03:47) -> 73 at 03:48 -> 95 at 03:49, then stayed flat; i.e. 59 failed checkout POSTs and about 60 ingress error spans, concentrated in the 03:47-03:49 sample interval.

Every failed checkout POST corresponds to a failed RPC chain: frontend's grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder client counter equals its POST /api/checkout counter (36 -> 73 -> 95 errors; UNSET 1140 -> 1150 -> 1191), while checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge counters are identical (UNSET 1140 at 03:47 and 03:48, 1149 at 03:49; ERROR series first appears at 37 at 03:48, reaches 59 at 03:49, then never increases), so 59 of the failures are failed Charge calls made by checkout.

Payment's own server-side Charge counters show no error status and a serving gap: payment span 'charge' and 'grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' are STATUS_CODE_UNSET throughout, 1140 at 03:47, 1140 at 03:48, 1150 at 03:49, 1191 at 03:50 (no Charge served in the 03:47->03:48 interval), and payment had 0 error spans and 383 UNSET 'charge' spans in the 22-minute window.

The payment Deployment was rolled at 03:46:08-03:46:11: Deployment payment 'Scaled up replica set payment-7b6bfb9fb4 from 0 to 1' at 03:46:08, ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4 'Created pod: payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht' at 03:46:08, pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 'Killing/Stopping container payment' and ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 'SuccessfulDelete' at 03:46:11, and 'Scaled down replica set payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0' at 03:46:11. All other otel-demo pods started at 03:13 with restartCount 0.

Pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht was created 2026-11-15T03:46:08Z, owned by ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4, with condition Ready=True at 03:46:11Z, container started 03:46:11Z, restartCount 0, lastState empty, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment (imageID sha256:342c8ce5e0cf68f9c67a2e932a886eeba9dc6d21e615e0f2bc12a305ee09dc6e).

The only pod-template difference between payment ReplicaSet revision 1 (payment-55766d76b9) and revision 2 (payment-7b6bfb9fb4) is the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-15T03:46:08Z; image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, all env vars, ports, resources and securityContext are identical, so this was a rollout restart, not an image or configuration change. Deployment payment is at generation 2 / revision 2, while frontend, checkout and frontend-proxy are at generation 1.

Deployment payment runs replicas=1 with readinessProbe, livenessProbe and startupProbe all null, RollingUpdate maxSurge/maxUnavailable 25%; checkout, frontend and frontend-proxy likewise define no probes.

The new payment container logged nothing between its start at 03:46:11 and 03:48:18.976Z: the earliest line of pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht inside 03:46:00-03:49:40 is 03:48:18.976Z ('Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.'), so it handled no Charge requests for about 2 minutes after being marked Ready.

The payment log lines read for pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht in 03:45:00-04:07:27 consist only of the pairs 'Charge request received.' and 'Transaction complete.', with no other message type present in the 605 lines read; the newest read line is 2026-11-15T03:56:18.028Z.

The failed Charge calls were fast, not timeouts: the duration histogram of checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge span shows 244.48/334.48 calls at or below 10 ms and 331.15/334.48 at or below 1000 ms during 03:45:27-03:55:27, versus 308.42/360 at or below 10 ms and 355.79/360 at or below 1000 ms during the 03:35:27-03:45:27 baseline.

The error rate increase is large against the in-window baseline: frontend-proxy's error ratio was 0.000725 and 0.000199 for the 15-minute windows ending 03:45:27Z, while during 03:45:27-03:55:27 the ingress operation recorded 70 error spans against 6848.89 UNSET spans (about 1.0%), matching the alert annotation's 0.0111.

checkout recovered after the payment pod started serving: checkout logs from 03:51:47Z show '[PlaceOrder]', 'payment went through', 'order placed' and Kafka 'Successful to write message', payment logs continue successful charges through 03:56:18Z, and both the checkout and frontend error counters are flat from the 03:49:00 sample onward.

ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo currently sets the fault-injection flag paymentFailure to defaultVariant '100%' with state ENABLED (variants include '100%': 1 and 'off': 0); all other demo failure flags (adFailure, cartFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, etc.) are at defaultVariant 'off'.

Only traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket exist for service_name payment and checkout in this datasource; no rpc_client_duration/rpc_server_duration or http_*/envoy_* series are present, and the span metrics carry no HTTP status code or status message label (labels on the frontend-proxy series are __name__, container, endpoint, exported_*, instance, job, le, namespace, otel_scope_name, pod, prometheus, prometheus_replica, service, service_name, span_kind, span_name, status_code).

Primary cause: the error burst is a consequence of the payment Deployment rollout restart at 03:46:08. Because payment is a single replica with no readiness probe, the new pod was reported Ready at 03:46:11 while its process handled no requests until 03:48:18.976; checkout's 59 Charge RPCs in that gap had no matching payment server span, failed in under a second, and cascaded into 59 failed PlaceOrder/checkout POSTs and about 60 frontend-proxy ingress error spans, lifting frontend-proxy's error ratio to about 1% (the alert's 0.0111). The transport-level error code itself is not observable in the available data.

Alternative candidate that the non-default flagd flag paymentFailure='100%' made payment reject charges is not supported by the observed data: payment recorded zero error spans (its 'charge' and 'grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' spans are all STATUS_CODE_UNSET), it made no grpc.flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveFloat calls in the window (count 0 for both status variants), and every charge it logged after 03:48:18.976 completed with 'Transaction complete.'

The hypothesis that frontend-proxy itself or other downstream services (ad, cart, currency, shipping, product-catalog, email, accounting) failed and pulled the proxy's error rate up is not supported: the proxy's error spans are limited to 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress', the error-span counters are confined to the checkout path (frontend POST /api/checkout and grpc PlaceOrder, checkout PlaceOrder and Charge), accounting and payment show 0 error spans, and ad/fraud-detection/recommendation show only baseline-level counts (about 1.06 errors in 22 minutes).

Evidence that limits how far the alert's timing can be tied to the rollout: the alert's stated startsAt is 2026-11-15T03:45:51Z, before the new payment ReplicaSet existed (created 03:46:08Z) and before the old payment pod was killed (03:46:11Z); the sampled frontend-proxy error counter was still flat (489) at the 03:45 sample and only 490 at 03:46, so the counter evidence cannot show a failing request before 03:46:08Z. The alert's reported value 0.0111 matches the ~1% ratio computed over 03:45:27-03:55:27, but the alert's own evaluation window is not verifiable.

Add a readinessProbe (or startupProbe) that hits the payment container's listening port, and/or run more than one payment replica with maxUnavailable 0, so a rollout restart cannot send traffic to a pod whose process is not yet accepting connections; the current single-replica, probe-less configuration is what turned a routine restart at 03:46:08 into failed checkouts.

Ask the operator why 'kubectl rollout restart' was applied to deployment/payment at 03:46:08Z (the only template change is kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt), and reset or re-verify flagd-config's paymentFailure flag, which now reads '100%' instead of the demo default 'off', once change history is available.

gaps: Jaeger returned no_data for every trace query in this Run (frontend-proxy, checkout, frontend and load-generator service searches and an error=true tag search), so span tags, error messages and parent-child call edges for the failed checkouts are unknown; the exact gRPC status code (e.g. UNAVAILABLE vs CANCELLED/DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) on checkout's Charge call is not observable.

The datasource exposes no HTTP status code, gRPC status code or rpc_*/http_* metrics (only traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket), and label-name exploration for __name__ matching http_.*/envoy_*/app_.*/kube_.* returned no_data, so it cannot be confirmed that the failing POST /api/checkout requests returned 5xx rather than 4xx.

Prometheus has no rules loaded: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name RequestErrorRate and with type=alert both returned no_data, so the alert's expression, evaluation window, threshold and current firing/recovered state cannot be verified; the alert's 0.0111 value and 03:45:51Z start are taken from the supplied alert payload only.

Metric samples in this datasource begin around 03:27-03:30Z and end around 03:56-03:58Z: there is no pre-incident baseline before ~03:27Z and no coverage of 03:58-04:07Z, so the error rate during the last ~10 minutes of the authorized window is unknown. The error-rate baseline is therefore an in-window comparison only.

No logs are available from the terminated payment pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 (previous container instance unavailable) and the previous payment container in the new pod does not exist, so why payment served nothing between 03:46:11 and 03:48:18.976 (application startup vs. endpoint/connection propagation) cannot be determined.

The error-keyword filter over payment's logs (err|error|fail|exception|panic|refused|deadline|unavailable) returned no_data rather than an ok view, so the absence of error text in payment's logs cannot be asserted as a fact; only the presence of successful charge lines is established, and the filtered read removed 605 of 605 lines without a citable assertion that no error line exists.

The equivalent error-keyword filter over checkout's logs (err|error|fail|exception|rpc|refused|deadline|unavailable|code) also returned no_data, so no application-level error message from checkout was observed to confirm the transport failure mode, and the checkout log payload beyond the unfiltered 03:51:47+ samples is unknown.
A trace search in the Jaeger backend for services (and the load-generator) returned no_data as well, so the caller side of the failed requests (load-generator traffic mix) is unknown.

change_history is not an integrated source, and Kubernetes objects/configmaps show only current state; who or what initiated the payment rollout restart at 03:46:08Z, and whether flagd-config's paymentFailure value differed during the incident window, cannot be verified. Secrets are unreadable, and the old payment pod's image digest cannot be compared with the new pod's sha256:342c8ce5...

The 22-minute aggregate for frontend (250.29 error spans) includes pre-window baseline errors (the frontend error counter was already 36 at 03:40), so the exact count of non-checkout frontend error spans in the incident window could not be separated.

Several metric/exploration views in this Run returned no_data and therefore establish nothing about the entities they targeted: get_series and get_all_labels for rpc_client_duration/rpc_server_duration, and the traces_search_by_tags error=true query — their emptiness is unknown, not zero.
next_steps: Add a readiness/startup probe to the payment container (and consider 2+ replicas with maxUnavailable 0) so restart-induced unavailability cannot surface as checkout errors.
Confirm with the operator or change record why deployment/payment was rollout-restarted at 2026-11-15T03:46:08Z, and whether the single alert at ~03:45:51Z was the trigger for that restart.
Review flagd-config's paymentFailure='100%' setting and decide whether it should be returned to 'off'; verify separately whether the payment service actually evaluates that flag during Charge.

When trace retention or a longer Jaeger store is available, retrieve a failed checkout trace from 03:47-03:49Z to capture the exact gRPC status code and error message on checkout's PaymentService/Charge client span, which would confirm the transport-level failure mechanism.
Extend Prometheus retention (or query a longer-lived store) so a true pre-incident baseline of frontend-proxy's error ratio exists for future alert tuning.
